 In The High Court Of Judicature At Patna
 Criminal Appeal (Sj) No.4246 of 2023
 Arising Out of Ps. Case No.-209 Year-2018 Thana- Harlakhi District- 
 ======================================================
 Jayveer Raut, son of Ramvilash Raut, resident of village - Kauaha,

======================================================
 Appearance :
 For the Appellant/s : Mr.Gagandeo Yadav, Advocate
 Mr.Ravi Prakash, Advocate
 Mr.Rajesh Kumar, Advocate
 For the Respondent/s : Mr.Anand Mohan Prasad Mehta, Addl.P.P.
 ======================================================
 Coram: Honourable Mr. Justice Chandra Shekhar Jha
 Oral Order
4 11-12-2024
Heard learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant and learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State.

2. Present prayer of bail along with suspension of sentence under Section 389(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure (hereinafter referred to as the "Cr.P.C.")/Section 430(1) of the Bhartiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (in short the "B.N.S.S.") which has been raised through memo of appeal itself as preferred under Section 374(2) of the Cr.P.C./Section 415(2) of the B.N.S.S. against the judgment of conviction dated 09.08.2023 and order of sentence dated 19.08.2023 passed by learned Additional Sessions Judge-VII-cum-Special Judge, POCSO, Madhubani in connection with Tr. No.
86/2023, POCSO G.R. Case Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.4246 of 2023(4) dt.11-12-2024 No.
90/2018 (arising out of Harlakhi P.S. Case No. 209 of 2018) whereby appellant has been convicted for the offence under section 376 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 4 of the POCSO Act and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for ten (10) years and fine of Rs. 15,000/-, in default of payment of fine, further S.I. for six months.

Further, the appellant convicted for the offence under Section 363 of the I.P.C. and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for three years and fine of Rs. 5,000/-, in default of payment of fine, further to undergo S.I. for three months and thereafter,
the learned trial court ordered that both the sentences shall run concurrently.

sentences.text: It is submitted by Mr. Gagandeo Yadav, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant/convict that learned trial court completely ignored the statement of victim as recorded under Section 164 of the Cr.P.C. and also her testimony as PW-1.

It is submitted that the version of victim, as it appears out of her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. and also out of her testimony as PW-1 that physical relation was established with the appellant out of her consent after performing their marriage at Bangaluru.

4. It is pointed out that merely considering the fact that victim, as per her birth certificate issued by Department of Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.4246 of 2023(4) dt.11-12-2024 Planning and Development, Government of Bihar, where her date of birth shown as 06.09.2003, was declared below the age of 18 years, though the doctor/PW-7 found her age about 18 years.

entities.text: Planning and Development, Government of Bihar
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In this context, it is further submitted that victim herself deposed during trial that she appeared in Class-Xth examination, but despite of that no certificate from her first standing school was brought on record in terms of Section 94(2)(i) of Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, as approved by Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Jarnail Singh v. State of Haryana reported in (2013) 7 SCC 263, as in absence of said document, the document in support of birth issued by the Corporation or Municipal Authority or Panchayat can be taken note of.

entities.text: Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act
entities.label: STATUTE

entities.text: Jarnail Singh v. State of Haryana reported in (2013) 7 SCC 263
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is submitted that in view of same, it can also be said that the victim could not proved 'child' within the meaning of Section 2(1)(d) of the POCSO Act, 2015.

5. While concluding argument, it is submitted that with aforesaid evidence, it can be said safely that balance of appeal is in favour of appellant/convict, where appellant remains in custody for about two years and four months against fixed term sentence of ten (10) years and as this appeal is of September 2023 itself and same is not likely to be heard finally in near future, therefore, on this ground alone, appellant/convict deserves bail.

Patna High Court CR. APP (SJ) No.4246 of 2023(4)
dt.11-12-2024 6.

In support of submission, learned counsel for the appellant relied upon the legal report of Hon'ble Supreme Court as available through Atul alias Ashutosh Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh [(2024) 3 SCC 663] and the Hon'ble Full Bench judgment of this Court as available through Anurag Baitha Vs.
State of Bihar reported in AIR 1987 Pat 274(FB).
7.

entities.text: Atul alias Ashutosh Vs. State of Madhya Pradesh [(2024) 3 SCC 663]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text:
Anurag Baitha Vs.
State of Bihar reported in AIR 1987 Pat 274(FB)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned A.P.P. for the State, while opposing the prayer of bail and suspension of sentence of the appellant/convict, submitted that victim categorically testified that she established physical relation with appellant/convict on multiple occasion, however, he could not disputed the submissions as advanced on behalf of the appellant/convict, including custody period.

8. In view of aforesaid factual submissions and by taking note of testimony of victim/PW-1 in totality, coupled with the fact that appellant remains in custody for about two years and four months against fixed term sentence of ten (10) years and further this appeal is not likely to be heard in near future as the same is of September 2023 itself, accordingly, appellant/convict above-named is directed to be released on bail, during pendency of this appeal, on furnishing bail bond of Rs.
10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand only) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Additional Sessions Judge-VII-cum-Special Patna High Court CR.
